When Karl (John Hannah) awakes in a wrecked hotel room with a splitting headache, it isn’t because he’s nursing a nasty hangover. Karl has no memory of what’s happened, where he is, or even who he is.

When he discovers a dead body in his bathtub, and two police officers soon knocking at his door, it sets into motion a terrifying and explosive series of events that force Karl and hotel maid Molly (Radha Mitchell) on a blind descent into a deceptive world of confusion and conspiracy, all the while with a price on his head and half the city in murderous pursuit.

Karl will need to draw on his forgotten skill sets if he has any hope of survival, as he and Molly endeavour to unravel the mystery that took his memories.

Shot entirely in first person, Bad Day At The Office combines a high-octane action thriller with that of an adrenaline-fueled video game. With the action all seen through the eyes of the protagonists via GoPro cameras; every punch, every chase, every explosion is seen and felt. For fans of Hardcore Henry, blended with Crank, Call of Duty, and sprinkling of Guy Ritchie's Snatch, this is John Hannah (The Mummy) as you've never seen him.

Bad Day at the Office also stars Radha Mitchell (Pitch Black), Tamer Hassan (The Football Factory) and Lana Parrilla (Once Upon a Time) as well as Tim Fellingham (Final Destination 5), Roxanne McKee (Game of Thrones), Branko Tomović (24: Live Another Day) and Victor Gardener (Fast and Furious 6).

Director Chee Keong Cheung has created a wild and relentless POV thriller that puts the audience squarely inside the chaos. You are not watching the main character. You are the main character.

articles.title: Brandon Sanderson Talks Blightfall, Wheel of Time, and Games of Thrones in Exclusive Interview
articles.summary: In an exclusive interview with IGN, Brandon Sanderson discusses his new book Blightfall, reflects on the Wheel of Time cancellation "tragedy", and defends George R.R. Martin, explaining that, if asked, he wouldn't say yes to finishing the Song of Ice and Fire books.
articles.body:
Brandon Sanderson has long been one of our favourite go-to authors at IGN, and recently we had the pleasure of chatting with the bestselling author for an exclusive interview.

From the epic Cosmere Universe to his latest collaboration with co-writer Janci Patterson – Blightfall, which just so happens to be one of our best books of September 2026 – it’s safe to say we’ve become fully immersed in the fantastical worlds Sanderson has crafted.

But if you’ve ever wondered how he balances multiple projects at once, or where he gets his inspiration, he’s sharing all with us. We might even be a little closer to finding out what to expect from the first Mistborn movie, possible video game adaptation of his books, alongside new insights from Sanderson on Wheel of Time and George R.R. Martin's A Song of Ice and Fire.

Blightfall marks your second release of 2026 so far. How do you balance writing across several different stories and books at once?

Brandon Sanderson: It's always a bit of a challenge! Back when I was an aspiring author, I could just write whatever I felt like, abandoning projects if I wasn't interested any longer. As a professional, I do still abandon books, but the threshold is much higher – you need to learn to push through the difficult parts, rather than just taking the easy path.

Sometimes, one of those difficult parts is juggling multiple projects. I usually only write new material on one book at a time, but often a book (like Blightfall) will bounce back to me from Janci for a read while I'm in the middle of something else. During those months, I generally take a break from the book I was writing and dedicate full time to the revision, because otherwise these deadlines tend to slip away from you.

Do you ever see yourself slowing down at some point? Or, alternatively, do you have many more ideas on the go/in the works going forward?

Sanderson: The great tragedy of art, I have found, is that there's never time – and never will be time – to do all the things you want to do. I have to be ready to make an expert triage of the stories I want to tell.

There's always a balance between supporting what I am already creating (like the Cytoverse) and new projects (like The Fires of December , my next release.) I don't see myself slowing down, but the creative process is unpredictable. As are publication schedules. Sometimes, a book that has been in the process for many many years (like Songs of the Dead ) that I haven't touched much for four years suddenly gets a release, and it makes me seem a little more prolific than I am. People forget the years with one (or even zero) books released.

Sanderson: An absolute delight. I've collaborated with her many times, and she really adds something to the stories. I go to Janci when there's a vibe or feel for a story I'm just not quite landing, and I think her voice will fix it. Like it did this time.

Why did you opt to go down the 'young adult' route with Blightfall?

Sanderson: Skyward straddles that line between young adult and adult. It was published as YA in the US, and adult in the UK. However, my intention was always to have it skew a tad younger than my other books – if only because the story is about teens who are forced, before their time, into leadership roles on a planet where war has claimed the lives of much of the older population. This is an inherently YA premise, I feel, and it really matches the themes.

We know you shouldn’t have favourites, but is there one series or book that you view as your favourite? And why?

Sanderson: Nope! I won't be caught by you on that one. All of my children are equally loved.

How has your writing process changed over the years?

Sanderson: It's become increasingly more deliberate. The more I write, the more I recognize why I do what I do, and how best to grow.

As a new writer, I'd often do something that felt really great, then have the next scene fall apart – and I had terrible difficulty telling why one writing session worked and why another one did not. With twenty years as a professional under my belt, I find that I can better gauge what will work, and if it doesn't, the autopsy of why is more illustrative.

And where do you get your inspiration from?

Sanderson: This is a truly difficult question for me to answer, because it's everywhere. I often find myself asking the "what if?" questions that are classics to science fiction and fantasy. For these books, one of those questions was, "What if humans got into space. . .and didn't become a peaceful member of the community, but tried to conquer the galaxy?" Or, "What if that were your legacy? How would you go about changing?" Oftentimes I'm looking for a take on a question I haven't seen before in other media.

Get 4 Months of Audible Standard for $0.99/mo

You revealed earlier this year that Skyward is getting a TV series . How much are you thinking about TV adaptations as you expand the Cytoverse?

Sanderson: I never really think about adaptations when I'm writing the story. I figure, if the novel is good enough, we'll figure out a way to adapt it later – and indeed, film/TV are different enough mediums from books, I know there will need to be changes made.

I feel it would be madness to try to write a book to be "more adaptable." Again, they're different mediums, so I want to write the story in the best way to match the medium.

You've put out some great Cosmere tabletop collabs with Brotherwise Games over the past few years, do you plan on doing the same thing with the Cytoverse?

Sanderson: I would love to! We've talked about it. However, I also want to be aware of asking my fans for too much.

There are a lot of great books out there, and a lot of great games. I don't want or need it to be all Brandon Sanderson all the time. We try to be very deliberate and careful about these kinds of collaborations, to only be doing what will feel the most exciting to my fans.

Speaking of tabletop adaptations of your work, have you given any thought as to what a video game adaptation of any of your books could look like?

Sanderson: As a lifelong gamer, suffice it to say that yes, I've thought about this a lot. The key will be the right partner. Video games, even the smaller indie games, are huge investments these days. Mistborn would almost certainly be the first thing I would try, as the mechanics of the magic and world very naturally lend themselves to such an adaptation – but again, I'd need the right partner.

We're very excited for the first Mistborn movie, and you've recently said you finished the first draft of the screenplay for it . How many years away do you think it actually is until we get to see it?

Sanderson: Ha. That's an excellent question! I would imagine this is still many years off.

I have to finish revisions on it, then will begin the hunt for a director, which is probably the single most important decision that we'll make. Visual effects these days can take a good eighteen months on a big film, or more. So even once we've filmed (which I imagine is a few years away), it could be two years before the film is ready for release. So let's not get too far ahead of ourselves. Right now, my primary focus in that sphere is making the screenplay the best possible version of itself.

I know you shared a brief comment when Wheel of Time was canceled, but how do you reflect on the show now that the dust has settled?

Sanderson: It's a tragedy. In part for the cast and crew, whom I knew worked extremely hard, only to have their story end up unfinished. I don't know if it would ever be possible to get a better Moiraine than Rosamund, for example. At the same time, I wish I'd been able to persuade them to stick to the books in a few key aspects.

I'm not one who thinks nothing can ever change in an adaptation, but there were alterations made here that led to an ever widening gulf between Robert Jordan's vision and the show. I feel there was a way to do what Amazon wanted and what the fans wanted, and maintain a little more clarity as to the themes of the books.

Would you still be up for being involved with any adaptations in the future?

Sanderson: If they want me! They might not, as I was kind of loud behind the scenes about my dislike of some of these changes…

And do you continue to have any sort of relationship with the rights holders?

Sanderson: I have an excellent relationship with Harriet and her team. I'm publishing Wheel of Time leatherbound editions right now, and worked extensively with Harriet and Maria on perfecting those. I have not spoken to the tv/film rights holders in many years.

As an author, do you have any sympathies with George R. R. Martin potentially not being able to finish Game of Thrones — especially since George has described his mental health issues recently ?

Sanderson: Absolutely. I implore people, in this discussion, to remember the person.

George R. R. Martin is one of the greats of our genre, and in my every interaction with him, he's treated me with kindness – even when I was a nobody. He truly is the great patriarch of the fantasy genre, and has done a great deal of work fostering new talent, helping the community, and offering advice and support when needed.

At the same time, writing can be a lonely profession, and we all know the difficulty of a book that just WILL NOT work. I've been fortunate that books like that have always been side projects for me, ones I can abandon without it causing too many ripples in my career. The only thing that will lead to A Song of Ice and Fire being finished is our support, patience, and effort to remember what makes books special: the fact that they are one of the few mass media art forms that are still largely created by individual human beings.

Would you ever consider finishing it , as you did with Wheel of Time?

Sanderson: Respectfully, I'm the wrong person to do this – and I think most fans of both of our works would agree. My entire career is, in a way, a response to A Song of Ice and Fire. Much as that series is a response to popular fiction of the 1990s, like Wheel of Time.

If I were to say yes, I would do my best to write it exactly as fans want and expect, but I would not say yes – because there are much more natural fits out there, and if George decided to go that direction, he'd deserve someone who is as good a fit for his world as I was for Wheel of Time. That said, I don't think George wants to go that direction, so let's just support him in writing his books at the speed he's capable of going.

And do you think Martin owes anyone the final books?

Sanderson: This is an interesting question, but I think you're asking it in a slightly wrong way. (Though it is the way people often ask it.) George doesn't owe people books, as he cannot actually make that promise — none of us can.

I can't promise the end of the Stormlight Archive, because who knows if I'll come down with a sickness tomorrow. I am literally incapable of making promises about the future in that way, the same as any person is.That said, I do think we, as authors, are making a contract with readers when we start a book series – and that contract implies a certain responsibility on our part. The promise to work on the project, to give it due attention, to try our best to get the books done in a timely way. However, this is an art.

I am as guilty as anyone of, now and then, making light of the fact that we don't have a conclusion to Game of Thrones. However, I live in a glass house, as I have a book (The Rithmatist) that I've promised fans a sequel to for as long as people have been waiting for George's next volume. I feel terrible I haven't been able to deliver, but the artistic process can be a whimsical one.

Regardless, I don't know that George owes anyone books as much as he owes them real, dedicated effort in producing those books, which might seem like semantics, but I'm an author. That's the job. It's not, however, my job to determine if George has made that effort or not. My gut says that he has – and the fact that we're where we are indicates that this is one of those times when the rest of the world has to wrestle with a terrible fact we as authors face every day. That from the outside, this seems like a trade (like making cabinets) when in reality it's an art, much like making music… and sometimes, you lose that music. [Let's] just hope it's not forever.

And can you share any sneak peeks that we can look forward to, or something like an exclusive reveal for IGN readers?

Sanderson: The only book I have announced right now is The Fires of December, coming (appropriately) in December. This is a book in the same loose "series" as Tress of the Emerald Sea and Yumi and the Nightmare Painter . So imagine a little more of a "storytellerish" feel to it, like those books.

I'm extremely proud of it, and did a reading of the entire first chapter at Nexus last year. That's on YouTube, if people care to read it.

The Fires of December: A Cosmere Novel (Hoid's Travails)

Ellis is a freelance journalist, based in the UK, with a love of all things books. She also routinely chairs bookish events up and down the country, getting the scoop from some of the biggest and bestselling authors to keep you in the know.

articles.title: Lanterns Midseason Trailer for Last 3 Episodes Leaves Fans Feeling Like They've Got 2 Seasons in 1
articles.summary: HBO has released a midseason trailer for hit DC Universe show Lanterns, and it’s packed with tantalizing details on where the final three episodes will go.
articles.body:
HBO has released a midseason trailer for hit DC Universe show Lanterns , and it’s packed with tantalizing details on where the final three episodes will go.

Warning! Spoilers for Lanterns follow...

Early on, Lanterns set up the impending death of Kyle Chandler’s Hal Jordan, and based on this teaser, the show will see Aaron Pierre’s John Stewart try to solve the mystery of his murder. We see Sinestro here again, no doubt stewing the pot, as well as Nathan Fillion’s Guy Gardner. The show really has evolved into Lanterns, plural.

The blackest night is yet to come. Catch up on #Lanterns and stream new episodes Sundays on HBO Max. pic.twitter.com/1avM6N8Cdv — HBO Max (@hbomax) September 17, 2026

The blackest night is yet to come. Catch up on #Lanterns and stream new episodes Sundays on HBO Max. pic.twitter.com/1avM6N8Cdv

There’s so much to talk about here. Stewart and Jordan have a catch-up after the dramatic events of last Sunday’s episode, which left both without the Green Lantern ring (Stewart by choice, Jordan because it was taken from him). It sounds like they will continue to be at each other’s throats during the rest of the season. Guy Gardner shows up to talk to Stewart, who is behind bars. “I can’t help you solve this murder,” Gardner tells Stewart. “It’s bad optics.” why is Stewart in jail in the first place?

We also see Sinestro saying “Hal didn’t have to die in vain… I know a way.” Is this some sort of resurrection plan? Something else? Whatever it is, I’m sure Sinestro’s plan is nefarious and very very yellow.

Through all this is the mystery of Noah Macon, born to lawyer Billy Macon and Sheridan County Sheriff's Department sheriff Kerry Kane. The last episode hinted that his conception may have been a "miracle" performed by the Manhunter. If so, does he have a bit of Manhunter in him? In the final three episodes, we’ll see him older and playing as a quarterback for his high school football team. I’m sure Noah’s fate will be tied to the end of the series in some way.

Whatever the case, fans are praising the trailer for making it feel like Lanterns is two seasons in one. The last episode really did feel like a season ender, and based on these final three episodes, we’re jumping forward significantly — and closer in time to last summer’s DCU kickstarter, Superman.

“I feel Hal isn't actually dead the way this trailer makes it out,” one fan on the Lanterns subreddit said. “I'm ready for the twists!!” “Don't die don't die don't die,” another pleaded. “This trailer focuses too much on his death. Any one else feel that? It's like they REALLY want us to believe he’s dead,” another pondered. “Or am I just coping?”

While we wait to find out, check out IGN’s review of Lanterns Episode 5 .

Wesley is Director, News at IGN. Find him on Twitter at @wyp100. You can reach Wesley at wesley_yinpoole@ign.com or confidentially at wyp100@proton.me.

articles.title: Pokémon Trading Card Store Denies Giving Special Treatment to Celebrities, as Angry Customers Leave a Flood of Negative Reviews
articles.summary: A British Pokémon card store has denied giving celebrities special treatment during a 30th Anniversary Pokémon card launch that left customers who had queued for hours empty handed.
articles.body:
A British Pokémon card store has denied giving celebrities special treatment during a 30th Anniversary Pokémon card launch that left customers who had queued for hours empty handed.

Geek Retreat Chelmsford, a gaming and collectible retailer in southern England, was one of the thousands of stores to hold a special opening yesterday, in order to sell the latest set of highly sought after Pokémon cards.

Alongside hundreds of average shoppers, however, were a pair of notable UK figures: Stacey Solomon and Joe Swash, a reality TV star couple seen on shows such as The X Factor, Dancing on Ice, and I'm a Celebrity... Get Me Out of Here!

In a widely-shared video posted online, the situation outside Geek Retreat Chelmsford can be seen descending into chaos, as shoppers discover the store's stock has rapidly sold out. Numerous posts from customers via X/Twitter and Facebook claim that they had been told told by staff not to queue or park directly outside before opening in order to deter scalpers — but that this did not apply when Solomon and Swash turned up, and reported parked directly in front of the store.

"They parked right outside, skipped the queue and bought most of the stock, leaving about 10 items for the 200+ people still waiting," wrote WeLovePokémon, a fan account with more than 82,000 followers.

Worst 30th Celebration story I’ve seen. Geek Retreat Chelmsford told customers they weren’t allowed to queue until 30 mins before opening, they weren’t allowed to park outside the shop, and there would be a 1pp limit. All of that went out the window when two celebrities (Joe… pic.twitter.com/j72bNCaFS2 — We Love Pokemon (@WeLovePokemon) September 17, 2026

Worst 30th Celebration story I’ve seen. Geek Retreat Chelmsford told customers they weren’t allowed to queue until 30 mins before opening, they weren’t allowed to park outside the shop, and there would be a 1pp limit. All of that went out the window when two celebrities (Joe… pic.twitter.com/j72bNCaFS2

However, Geek Retreat Chelmsford has now issued a statement to contest this account, call for calm as its Facebook page is flooded with negative reviews, and ask that its customers' anger not be directed at employees.

"We would like to address some of the negativity and aggression we have received today," the store wrote. "Today we ran the release of the Pokémon 30th Anniversary set in a way that we genuinely believed would best support our customers, maintain fairness and help reduce scalping. Unfortunately, we were never going to have enough stock to meet the demand, and we understand that this was disappointing for people who were unable to get everything they wanted.

"What we cannot accept, however, is that this disappointment has been directed towards our staff. Our staff work incredibly hard to make the shop a welcoming place for everyone. We are always happy to listen to genuine feedback, but abuse, aggression or threats towards our team are not acceptable under any circumstances. Anyone who has threatened or abused a member of our staff will not be welcome in our store.

"We would also like to address the suggestion that certain people, including well-known individuals, were given special treatment today. This is simply not true. We did not know that any famous people were attending until we saw them outside. They were not allowed in early, they were not given extra stock, and they were subject to exactly the same one of each product per-person limits as everyone else. They happened to be second in the queue when we opened, and no member of our team allowed them to skip the queue."

Despite the statement, the negative reviews remain. "30th celebrations release was a joke, store ordered 25 ETBs, chased customers down the road to prevent queuing which we all respected and understood as a method to combat scalping etc, yet quickly changed their minds when Joe Swash turned up, parked outside the store (another thing they said publically we were not to do) and then allowed him with his wife and multiple children to jump the queue and buy the majority of the stock. Outrageous display of poor management and poor choices, staff should be ashamed," reads one comment.

"Breaks protocol to sell to 'celebrities' who only purchased product to flip on their whatnot site, then makes a sob story post as if they're the victims when customers notice," wrote another.

"Horrendous behavior," wrote a third. "Everyone was told to not queue before 11.30am and do not loiter around the front of the shop, even in your motors. Joe Swash and Stacey Solomon, along with three other people, got out of their van, parked directly outside the shop, walked straight in past everyone and came out with half of the stock. Around 10 customers then came out with stock, until we had to be told by a customer who received nothing, that they were now out of stock. Hundreds of customers have been let down by you and your staff today."

Geek Retreat Chelmsford said it did allow some regular customers to pre-order stock, but acknowledged that there was simply no way to avoid some disappointment "when demand massively exceeds supply." No comment was made on where Swash and Solomon parked, or how many cards they and their children bought overall.

Yesterday, we reported on the long queues and the phenomenon of "ghost chairs" outside stores in the U.K., France, and the U.S. , as some fans waited in line for days ahead of the 30th Anniversary card set going on sale.

articles.title: Xbox’s clever disc-to-digital feature was 15 years in the making
articles.summary: Microsoft’s controversial Xbox One bets are paying off more than a decade later.
articles.body: When Xbox announced a new feature last month that lets you digitize existing physical game collections, I immediately thought of the Xbox One. Disc-to-digital seems like a clever new feature for Xbox, perfectly timed as a response to Sony killing PlayStation discs. But the reality is that it has been 15 years in the making and is now a big part of Xbox’s ongoing game preservation efforts. Ahead of the launch of the Xbox One in 2013, Microsoft made a key decision to uniquely identify discs. Sources familiar with Microsoft’s plans tell me the company was exploring the idea of true Xbox digital ownership in 2011, including digital gifting, recycling digital games, and the ability to swap discs at retail stores in exchange for a digital version. Some of those original Xbox One plans leaked out online, and many others have remained secret for more than a decade. Microsoft’s Xbox One launch hinted at some of these ideas, too. The console was originally supposed to be always online, to enable Microsoft’s vision of digital game sharing, and more. Microsoft walked back those plans after a messy and confusing Xbox One launch created a backlash to the always-online requirement. But some of those original digital ideas are now starting to come to life in different ways. Microsoft’s decision to essentially embed a serial number on the discs that Xbox consoles can read has allowed it to launch disc-to-digital, a method that lets you turn a physical Xbox One disc into a digital copy simply by slotting it into a disc drive. A decision made 15 years ago has resulted in this useful feature and may well lead to true digital ownership in the coming years. It’s not something Sony can copy, either. Unless the PlayStation maker has been quietly adding metadata to its discs over the years, it will have to find another method to help PS5 owners move their physical collections over to the digital era. Microsoft thought ahead, not necessarily to disc-to-digital, but just about identifying discs so it was ready for when console games moved into an all-digital era. That era looks like it’s right around the corner, especially now that Sony has announced it’s killing PlayStation discs in 2028. Both Microsoft and Sony also ship digital-only variants of their consoles, and it’s clear from game sales numbers that most titles are purchased digitally these days. I fully expect Microsoft to follow Sony and eventually scrap Xbox discs, especially as the number of authorized manufacturers capable of producing physical media continues to shrink. That’s largely because almost every other form of media, from music to movies, has moved on from optical discs. The big difference with Xbox, though, is that Microsoft has always been obsessed with game preservation. In the same year that disc-to-digital is launching, Microsoft is also bringing original Xbox and Xbox 360 games to PC. The company has also spent years working on its backward compatibility program, to get as many games from the Xbox and Xbox 360 eras working on modern Xbox consoles. Game preservation is a central part of Project Helix, the next Xbox that could play every Xbox game ever made. It’s not an easy task to pull off game preservation, either. There are the complex technical challenges that need to be overcome, alongside licensing issues and the business challenges from publishers that decide how a game should be sold. Some of those technical challenges mean that not every single Xbox One disc will work with this new disc-to-digital feature. That could be because some early discs simply didn’t get pressed with the unique identifier. Microsoft warned its internal Xbox testers that “it all depends on how and when the disc was manufactured and it may not have the features we need for this program.” Discs that are slightly damaged might also not work with disc-to-digital, but run just fine otherwise. That’s why it’s important that Xbox is launching this right now — physical media decays over time. The licensing and business challenges are far more complicated. Publishers need to agree to disc-to-digital, and some could hold back. It appears that most are on board, and even Ubisoft games started showing up recently. We’ve seen a number of other games come online since Microsoft’s announcement, and the company has been clear that more will follow. The next challenge beyond disc-to-digital is solving digital ownership. If all we really own of a digital game is a license, I hope that one day those licenses can move freely across devices and platforms. I want to buy a single copy of a game and have that license follow me across Xbox, PlayStation, Nintendo, and PC. I also want to be able to gift or sell that license on different marketplaces, just as we’ve been able to do with physical discs at retailers for decades. Microsoft envisioned this true digital ownership future 15 years ago, and it has gradually taken steps toward making it a reality. I hope Xbox can eventually pull it off, but the solution will require publishers and platform owners to agree on a shared system for how game licenses are bought, transferred, gifted, and resold. That’s a much bigger challenge than simply getting rid of the disc. The pad * Microsoft announces Windows and Surface event for October 7th. Microsoft is heading to San Francisco next month, and I’ll be there too. More than two years since the last major Windows event, Microsoft is holding a Windows and Surface event that will include a “conversation on how local AI will shape the next chapter of the PC.” Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella will be in attendance, alongside Windows chief Pavan Davuluri. The surprise guest? Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. I wouldn’t be surprised if this event is mainly focused on RTX Spark PCs, and don’t be surprised to hear more about the Microsoft Surface Laptop Ultra pricing and availability. * The Gates Foundation says it’s spending $1 billion to expand access to AI. Over the next two years, the Gates Foundation plans to spend at least $1 billion on improving access to AI in education, healthcare, and agriculture. The funds will go toward creating AI datasets in more languages and making AI access more affordable. * Microsoft says ‘people matter more than AI’ following safety concerns. Microsoft published a 37-page AI code of conduct this week, in the midst of researchers warning that AI progress could outpace human control. Microsoft’s AI code of conduct makes it clear that “people matter more than AI,” and that AI models are not conscious and “should not be designed to imitate consciousness.” That’s a direct swipe at Anthropic, which has been pushing the idea of AI welfare and model consciousness lately. The code of conduct also commits to ensuring Microsoft’s own models will remain under human control and discourage “patterns of interaction that cause excessive reliance or emotional dependence.” * Microsoft adds Grok to Word, Excel, and PowerPoint. Microsoft added SpaceXAI’s Grok models to its Foundry service last year, and now it’s expanding access to Copilot itself. Grok models can now be used in Word, Excel and PowerPoint from the model picker interface for Microsoft Frontier users. Microsoft says it’s starting with a preview release to “gather feedback.” This means Office Copilot users can now pick between OpenAI’s GPT models, Anthropic’s Claude models, and SpaceXAI’s Grok models. * Microsoft issues emergency Windows 11 update to fix its record-breaking patch. Last week I reported on Microsoft’s record-breaking patch Tuesday, and it turns out that this giant set of fixes has caused some issues. Microsoft has had to release an out-of-band patch to fix folder shares on Hyper-V-based Linux virtual machines, Remote Desktop Services sessions, and some USB audio devices. These out-of-band updates used to be a rare occurrence, but there have already been eight this year alone. With AI models continuing to spot even more vulnerabilities in Windows, I can’t see this all slowing down anytime soon. In fact, I wouldn’t be surprised if October’s patch Tuesday breaks another record. * BlizzCon delivers the return of StarCraft, Diablo on Netflix, and Diablo V. StarCraft is returning in 2030, after more than decade of lying dormant. The new title, announced onstage at BlizzCon last weekend, will be an open-world shooter instead of a top-down real-time strategy game. Blizzard is also working on a new animated series of Diablo with Netflix, and teased that Diablo V is coming in spring 2029. * Microsoft is finally adding a setting for remapping the Copilot key. If you picked up an Arm-powered Copilot Plus PC over the past years, you may have noticed the new Copilot key that launches Microsoft’s digital assistant. The latest Release Preview builds of Windows 11 add a setting to change the AI key back to a control or context menu button, so you don’t accidentally hit it and launch Copilot. * Microsoft’s head of comms is leaving after almost 20 years. Frank Shaw, chief communications officer at Microsoft, is leaving the company at the end of the year. Shaw has been at the heart of Microsoft’s communications for 29 years — nearly 20 years as a Microsoft employee plus time at an external agency before that. He’s well-respected across the public relations industry, and has earned a reputation both inside and outside Microsoft as someone who is direct but respectful. Many employees have told me over the years that they always fear an email from him for misspeaking or accidentally leaking product plans. Microsoft hasn’t appointed a replacement yet, but it sounds like a successor will be named in the coming weeks. * Xbox picks up Kojima’s Physint after PlayStation dropped it. Xbox will now publish Physint, an upcoming game from Metal Gear creator Hideo Kojima, after PlayStation decided to cancel it. The unexpected swap came in a flurry of announcements from PlayStation, Xbox, Kojima Productions, and Kojima. While PlayStation framed the swap as a “difficult decision to step away from collaborating with Kojima Productions,” Kojima revealed it was actually due to an unexpected cancellation notice for Physint in June. The swap now means Xbox is publishing the studio’s next game, OD, as well as Physint. It’ll be interesting to see what exclusivity decisions are made here. * Xbox is bringing back startup animations from its console history. Microsoft has started testing a new Xbox console feature that lets you enable the original Xbox One or Xbox One X boot screens on an Xbox Series S or X console. The update also includes a new search feature, improved Remote Play quality, and clearer voice chat. It’s great to see Xbox continue on its regular monthly console updates. * Microsoft has new AI privacy rules for schools. Microsoft agreed to a set of safety and privacy principles for AI in schools a week after two major school systems announced a ban on student-facing AI. The agreement with the American Federation of Teachers (AFT), the second-largest teachers union in the US, sees Microsoft commit to 10 principles that can be contractually enforced. This includes limits on the amount of data Microsoft collects from students or educators and a pledge not to train AI models on this data. New York City and Los Angeles have both implemented one-year bans on AI tools for lots of students, giving the districts more time to consider guardrails. * Microsoft’s Windows chief wants to remake Windows for both human and agent users. Pavan Davuluri, head of Windows and devices at Microsoft, caused some controversy when he tweeted last year that Windows was an agentic OS. That made many think Microsoft was abandoning Windows users in favor of AI, but Davuluri is now making things a lot clearer in an interview with GeekWire’s Mary Jo Foley. “The user of Windows going forward will continue to be users … but it’s also going to add these agentic workloads,” said Davuluri. “There is no one single sort of ring for a billion-plus users on the platform.” * Blizzard workers secure a major union contract. The nearly 1,900 workers across Blizzard have secured a contract with Microsoft that include “really strong” layoff protections. The World of Warcraft unit had to fight for a contract, and the teams that work on Overwatch, Diablo, quality assurance, and more helped put the pressure on to extend the union contract to all Blizzard employees. It comes just two months after Xbox announced significant layoffs that will impact 3,200 employees over the course of the current financial year. * The woman fixing a Microsoft mess with brutal honesty. The Wall Street Journal has published a profile of Xbox CEO Asha Sharma. It’s mostly a recap of Sharma’s career and how she got the top Xbox job, but it also includes some funny anecdotes. Surprisingly, Sharma spends a few hours each month personally responding to Xbox customer support tickets to better understand players. Since becoming Xbox CEO, she’s also received wedding invitations in the mail, presumably from the same fans that paste her face on images of Jesus Christ. Note: There won’t be a Notepad issue next week as I’m out for part of the week. I’m always keen to hear from readers, so please drop a comment here, or you can reach me at notepad@theverge.com if you want to discuss anything else. If you’ve heard about any of Microsoft’s secret projects, you can reach me via email at notepad@theverge.com or speak to me confidentially on the Signal messaging app, where I’m tomwarren.01. articles.title: Brandon Sanderson Says the Mistborn Movie Is 'Still Many Years Off' Despite a Finished First Draft
articles.summary: How long will we have to wait for the Mistborn Movie? We asked Brandon Sanderson for an update.
articles.body:
Ever since Brandon Sanderson revealed his partnership with Apple TV to adapt his Cosmere universe, he's been very transparent about the process. He's given regular updates via his YouTube channel, though he has consistently stated that it will be a while until we can actually watch this movie.

But how long exactly will we have to wait? IGN had the chance to interview Sanderson and ask him just how far away he thinks the Mistborn adaptation actually is. His answer, while disappointing for fans of the Cosmere books , is about what you'd expect.

"I would imagine this is still many years off," Sanderson told IGN. "I have to finish revisions on it, then will begin the hunt for a director, which is probably the single most important decision that we'll make. Visual effects these days can take a good 18 months on a big film, or more. So even once we've filmed (which I imagine is a few years away), it could be two years before the film is ready for release. So let's not get too far ahead of ourselves. Right now, my primary focus in that sphere is making the screenplay the best possible version of itself."

Going off of Sanderson's comments here, it seems like it could be a really long wait for the Mistborn movie to actually come to fruition. The timeline he laid out would suggest that it could be almost five years until Apple TV and Sanderson's team are actually able to produce a movie. That would mean we may not even see the film until 2031.

These are, of course, only estimates based on Sanderson's understanding of Hollywood and just how long everything takes, but it's the most specific timeline we've gotten from the author so far. For fans who have been hyped since the original announcement back in February of this year , that's a surprisingly long time to wait.

The good news is that while Sanderson's movie adaptation is still a long ways off, his next book in the Mistborn series is coming a lot sooner. After finishing his first draft of the Mistborn movie, the author confirmed that he's started up work again on the first book in Mistborn Era 3, titled Ghost Bloods. This era is expected to take place well in the future of Scadriel and is set to release in December 2028.

articles.title: First Look at David Bowie-Inspired Aslan in Greta Gerwig's 'Rock-Opera' Narnia: The Magician's Nephew
articles.summary: Narnia: The Magician's Nephew sounds like a very different movie than most expected.
articles.body:
Narnia: The Magician’s Nephew sounds like a very different movie than most expected.

The upcoming fantasy blockbuster directed by Barbie's Greta Gerwig will be exclusive to theaters from its release on February 12, with IMAX previews beginning on February 10, before hitting Netflix on April 2.

“I wanted a rock opera. I wanted it to be big and transporting,” Gerwig said in an interview with Empire to discuss the “ground-up retelling” of C. S. Lewis’ stories. The movie does not adapt the much-loved classic The Lion, The Witch And The Wardrobe, but the Narnia origin story. It isn’t set in the early 1900s, but post-war ‘50s Britain.

Narnia: The Magician’s Nephew is not a musical, but it is inspired by rock opera, in particular British rock from the ‘60s and ‘70s. So, expect lots of Bowie-style glam.

“Narnia is literally a world made out of music,” Gerwig said. “It is a world sung to life by Aslan, and rock ’n’ roll to me felt like a world made out of music.”

Meanwhile, Netflix released a first-look at Aslan, the powerful cosmic lion who sings Narnia into existence with his magnificent song. Gerwig’s take on Aslan is directly inspired by Bowie’s most famous character, Ziggy Stardust, complete with heterochromic eyes and a red-striped visage. He’s voiced by Meryl Streep.

“I wanted someone who was profound but not pretentious, who had gravitas but not morose self-seriousness,” Gerwig said. “Someone who could communicate depth and pathos as well as joy and delight. I wanted someone who was older than 70, so there was a wisdom of experience, but who also had the capacity of fresh wonder, like a child. And also to be one of the greatest actors to ever do it. That list is not a long one.”

The Magician's Nephew is chronologically the first book in C. S. Lewis' beloved Narnia series , though most adaptations to date have begun with The Lion, The Witch and The Wardrobe — the first Narnia story published, and by far the most famous. Indeed, The Magician's Nephew has never been adapted for the screen until now.

Clearly, though, Netflix hopes that this fresh entry point into the franchise will be a successful start to its plans for the series, with an all-star cast and years of work to bring the story to life. Carey Mulligan, Daniel Craig, Emma Mackey, Ciarán Hinds and the aforementioned Meryl Streep all feature in the film, with its young leads played by newcomers David McKenna and Beatrice Campbell.

Wesley is Director, News at IGN. Find him on Twitter at @wyp100. You can reach Wesley at wesley_yinpoole@ign.com or confidentially at wyp100@proton.me.

articles.title: Brandon Sanderson is Eager to Adapt His Books into a Video Game, Calling Himself a 'Lifelong Gamer'
articles.summary: “Lifelong gamer” Brandon Sanderson details his excitement about adapting Mistborn into a video game, explaining why its magic mechanics fit naturally. But only if he can find the right studio to partner with. Any takers?
articles.body:
During an exclusive interview with IGN, Brandon Sanderson has expressed interest in potentially adapting his Mistborn book series into a video game, but only if he can find the right studio to partner with.

Asked if he'd ever given any thought to a video game adaptation of his work, Sanderson said:

"As a lifelong gamer, suffice it to say that yes, I've thought about this a lot.

"The key will be the right partner. Video games, even the smaller indie games, are huge investments these days.

"Mistborn would almost certainly be the first thing I would try, as the mechanics of the magic and world very naturally lend themselves to such an adaptation – but again, I'd need the right partner."

So it doesn't sound like we'll be getting a Mistborn game anytime soon, but it's certainly on the cards for the distant future after Sanderson's recent comments.

This wouldn't be the first time Mistborn stepped out into other mediums either, with the Mistborn film adaptation in the works after Sanderson recently finished the screenplay ( but also saying there's "still a lot of work to do" ), alongside board games, and the recently released Cosmere RPG tabletop series that's soon getting a Mistborn expansion in November .

Mistborn Legacy Adventure - Cosmere RPG Campaign Guide

Mistborn Welcome to Scadrial - Cosmere RPG Guide

Developed by Brotherwise Games in close collaboration with Brandon Sanderson himself, the initial offerings for the Cosmere RPG focus solely on Roshar and the systems of the Stormlight Archive books. Now, Mistborn is joining the ranks with its Handbook, Campaign Guide, and Welcome to Scadriel guide which are all available to preorder now.

It's not a stretch to say that Mistborn could make for an exceptional RPG, akin to something like Baldur's Gate 3 . Moreover, Brotherwise Games has already done much of the groundwork with its impressive tabletop adaptation. There's clearly plenty there that could be built upon or adapted into a video game in the future.

For those who aren’t familiar with Mistborn, the Cosmere or Sanderson’s work in general, the Cosmere is a large galaxy-spanning, progressively more interconnected series of (mostly) epic fantasy novels by Brandon Sanderson. We have a comprehensive reading guide , so to find out more and get a better picture, and I suggest you head there and take a look.

You can read more of the big Brandon Sanderson interview here on IGN, where we've discussed the Wheel of Time cancellation, potentially finishing Game of Thrones , and his current progress on the Mistborn movie.

Robert Anderson is a Senior Commerce Editor for IGN. Based in London, UK, he is a qualified journalist with a Bachelor of Arts in Journalism (First Class Degree) and over seven years of professional writing and editing experience.

You can usually find Robert lost in open-world RPG games like Elden Ring and Cyberpunk 2077. Outside of gaming, his passions include reading comics (especially Superman, Batman, and Spider-Man), taking photos, and keeping up with the latest in film and TV.

His primary coverage focuses on tracking down the best gaming deals and diving into the fast-paced world of Trading Card Games (TCGs). He regularly covers everything from the latest releases in Pokémon TCG and the most expensive cards to comprehensive Magic: The Gathering buying guides .

For example, there aren't any themed consoles ( like there was for Wolverine ), there's no collector's edition outside of an album , and in fact even the "physical" edition of the game will just be a code in a box. However, one tangible limited edition piece of hardware you can acquire is the DualSense controller.

Walmart is currently offering preorders for the Grand Theft Auto Limited Edition PlayStation DualSense wireless gaming controller in white for $84.88 with free shipping. It's constantly going in and out of stock, although as of this article's publication it's available. Better yet, you can get an extra $10 on top by applying coupon code " SAVE3X ", dropping the price to $74.88. Your mileage may vary (it might not work for you) but we've confirmed that it is working for a lot of people. Here are the coupon code's official details:

Valid on your first three online pickup or delivery orders

Only for new customers (although it actually works for many returning customers)

and potentially get $10 off with code "SAVE3X"

Grand Theft Auto VI Limited Edition PlayStation 5 DualSense Wireless Controller

According to Sony , the limited edition controller “embodies Vice City at daybreak, from its white sands and pastel skies to all its laid-back glamour.” It features a two-tone white and iridescent purple/blue colorway, inset palm tree decorations, and a prominent GTA VI logo on the touch interface. It all looks pretty slick.

The DualSense is modeled after the tried and true design and layout of previous PlayStation controllers, but it also packs in modern features such as haptic feedback, adaptive triggers, a built-in microphone and speaker, integrated touchpad, internal gyroscope and accelerometer for motion sensing, and USB Type-C charging. This controller can also be connected to a PC in two ways: tethered with a USB Type-C cable or over Bluetooth wireless.

The Dualsense is often regarded as the best PS5 controller under $100 but it also makes for an excellent PC controller , especially since PC game clients like Steam support the DualSense's haptic feedback and adaptive triggers.

Grand Theft Auto 6 will be the biggest game release of 2026

GTA 6 has a confirmed release date of November 19, and I'm pretty convinced that no other game will be played on PlayStation or Xbox consoles in the days following. Just recently there has been a flood of new content for the game from our own exclusive interviews, Gamescom 2026 , and Netflix's exclusive extended look . This game will be the biggest release of 2026 and it just might be worth getting a PlayStation 5 for just one game if that game happens to be Grand Theft Auto 6.
